summary_oneline: Release escrow for the SDD flow: the worker emits work.completed, the feature is held until an external APPROVED verdict bound to its head SHA is recorded in the ledger, and /sdd-done refuses in code without it.

localization.role: host closeout pipeline; §4.6 is the model for a non-force-able code gate; §7 is the first mutation a verdict guard must precede; §9 is the force-able, --merge-only shape to avoid
Codex twin of /sdd-done; every gate change edits it together with the Claude command and the shipped asset
third twin shipped by the installer
worker end-of-feature protocol: review checkpoint → own code-reviewer → never push → optional desktop receipt → prints '✅ completed, run /sdd-done'; the seam where 'done' becomes work.completed
stdlib-only, sandbox-safe completion receipt bound to git HEAD with an all-tasks-done precondition and a one-shot host Stop hook; the ready-made emitter shape for work.completed
stamps the feature-level completed_at when the last task closes (worker grades itself) and already appends a task.closed LedgerEvent from inside the sandbox
closed Literal of 12 event kinds, content-addressed event_id, free-string actor, no signature; where work.completed and escrow.* kinds and payload models go
local journal ↔ committed sdd/ledger/events.jsonl; new kinds are shareable by default and travel cross-machine only once committed
only integrity check that exists: event_id matches content (FEAT-758 outbox delivery to the ledger branch)
the one human-only decision in the ledger today (actor must start with human:) and the feature-scoped blocker query /sdd-done §9 calls
strongest in-repo precedent for a verified approval: trust bound to the git commit that recorded it (commit, ancestry, actor, block hashes)
actor strings are resolved from env/context, not from a credential — any process can claim any actor
FEAT-764 dispatcher: exit 0/1/2/3, blocking pre_pr aborts, agent hooks go pending → record → finalize (host launches the subagent)
builtin registry (name → fn) plus one-way human notification channels usable to announce awaiting_verdict / escalation
.parrot/sdd_hooks.toml schema; hooks are repo-opt-in, so an escrow gate cannot rely on TOML alone
FEAT-703 standalone gate script whose exit code the twins obey; template for check_escrow_verdict
FEAT-584 head-bound review checkpoint (base_sha, implementation_head, exit 3 on stale) — the binding semantics a verdict needs; written by the worker, so evidence not verdict
host entry point `parrot sdd launch worker` → feature_launcher.launch; where --escrow[=policy] and a sibling verdict session attach
builds the worker sandbox/console and wires the notification env + Stop hook (TASK-5123)

per-spec index header (feature, feature_id, spec, type, base_branch, created_at, completed_at, parallel_semantics, validation_contract, test_contract) — the only feature-execution state; precedent for an escrow block
sdd/state/<FEAT>/state.json is proposal research state with additionalProperties:false — not an execution state file
/sdd-status reconciliation already derives 'dev considers the feature finished' from completed_at; an escrow line extends it
in-process async HITL approval (BLOCK/SUSPEND, fail-closed timeout, tiered EscalationPolicy); no host CLI; channels dormant since 2026-06
the only bus in-repo (navigator_eventbus Redis Streams, PARROT_ROOST_BUS_URL); unreachable from the worker sandbox and unused by SDD scripts
post-PR, Jira-keyed review layer escrow must not duplicate

constraints.statement: House rule for /sdd-done gates: the gate is a script, 'the exit code is the contract', and an un-bypassable gate takes no --force parameter at all (FEAT-703, FEAT-764).
constraints.implication: The verdict guard is a standalone check script run before §7, modelled on §4.6; no generic --force reaches it. Any human override is a separately recorded, human-actor ledger event, not a flag that skips the gate.

constraints.statement: Every /sdd-done gate change touches three twins (.claude command, .agents Codex skill, shipped asset) plus a tests/sdd_scripts/test_*_contract.py; the worker prompt has two byte-identical twins.
constraints.implication: Scope every integration task as twins + contract test; the twin test catches drift.

constraints.statement: LedgerEventKind is a closed Literal; event_id is a content hash; actor is a self-declared string resolved from env; nothing in the ledger is signed.
constraints.implication: work.completed and escrow.* require editing the Literal, payload models and the index reducer. 'Signed' is a new mechanism, not a field that exists.

constraints.statement: The only human-gated decision in the ledger is acknowledge (actor must start with human:) — a string-prefix check any process can satisfy.
constraints.implication: Separation of powers cannot rest on the actor string alone; it needs process separation (host-launched judge, sandboxed worker) and/or a host-only secret the worker cannot read.

constraints.statement: The worker sandbox cannot import parrot (stdlib-only helper run with python -S) but can write .parrot/ledger/; close_task already appends task.closed from inside it via an override interpreter.
constraints.implication: work.completed can be emitted from the worker side with the receipt's stdlib pattern, or on the host by the Stop hook that already consumes the receipt.

constraints.statement: The worker sandbox has no network beyond gh/api.github.com; the only bus is navigator_eventbus over Redis and no SDD script publishes to it; Squawk has no pub/sub API.
constraints.implication: v1 transport for work.completed is the ledger event log; a Redis bus is at most a v2 host-side mirror.

constraints.statement: Verdict events are shareable by default and travel through the FEAT-694 hooks / FEAT-758 outbox, but another machine sees them only after they are committed and imported.
constraints.implication: The guard must read the local journal and the committed log; a same-machine flow works immediately, cross-machine is eventual and must be stated.

constraints.statement: A verdict must be an event, never a snapshot edit; new kinds must flow through incremental sync, never the rebuild path that wipes spec:/task: pages.
constraints.implication: Only LedgerLog.append + reducer changes; no writes to issues.jsonl.

constraints.statement: No worker-owned state.json exists: sdd/state/<FEAT>/state.json is proposal research state (closed schema) and .autopilot/state.json is the autopilot tracker; the per-spec index header is the only feature-execution state and is untyped JSON.
constraints.implication: The requested AWAITING_VERDICT state cannot land in the existing state.json; it is either a header block, a new file, or a projection of ledger events.

constraints.statement: Head-binding precedents exist: the completion receipt validates HEAD on consumption and the review checkpoint exits 3 on checkpoint_stale when HEAD/base/spec/index hashes move.
constraints.implication: Bind the verdict to head_sha exactly as these do; a verdict for a different HEAD is stale, never approved.

constraints.statement: The worker already stamps the feature-level completed_at itself when the last task closes, and prints 'completed' plus 'run /sdd-done' as its final act.
constraints.implication: 'Done' today is literally self-declared; the contract change is to redefine these two moments as 'work completed, awaiting verdict'.

constraints.statement: Review already exists twice: the worker's own code-reviewer (same lineage) and /pr-review (post-PR, Jira-keyed).
constraints.implication: Escrow judges release readiness (completeness, head integrity, gates), not the diff; LLM re-review is optional and policy-driven, not the value.

constraints.statement: FEAT-764 agent hooks are host-dispatched: the session running /sdd-done launches the subagent and records the outcome.
constraints.implication: A judge launched that way is separate from the worker but not from the operator; acceptable for v1 and must be stated.

constraints.statement: HITL approval is an in-process async manager with Teams/Telegram channels untouched for five months; /sdd-done has one-way telegram.send / push.send builtins.
constraints.implication: v1 ESCALATE is notify + host CLI approve/reject writing a human: event; the manager is a v2 transport.

constraints.statement: /sdd-done §4.5 lint and §7 stamping commit on the feature branch; HEAD moves during the command.
constraints.implication: The guard must compare the verdict's head_sha with HEAD at gate time and run before any closeout commit, or lint reflows will make every verdict stale.

new.item: Ledger event kinds work.completed, escrow.approved, escrow.rescheduled, escrow.escalated, escrow.human_decision (+ payload models with feature_id, head_sha, launch_id, round, verdict_id)
new.role: the contract between worker, judge and /sdd-done; shareable, content-addressed

new.item: check_escrow_verdict script (parrot sdd escrow check) with a fixed exit-code contract and no force parameter
new.role: the /sdd-done guard: held unless an escrow.approved for the current HEAD exists for this feature and launch

new.item: Verdict model bound to head_sha (APPROVED | RESCHEDULE | ESCALATE_HITL), deterministic release actions
new.role: closed Pydantic model consumed by the action code, mirroring review_checkpoint's head binding

new.item: Host-side verdict runner: parrot sdd escrow run|show|approve|reject (+ a read-only .claude/agents/sdd-escrow.md judge with Codex twin)
new.role: produces the verdict outside the worker's session/sandbox; approve/reject is the human HITL fallback writing a human: event
deterministic opt-in per launch; records escrow enablement where the guard and status can read it and exports it to the worker env

new.item: sdd/escrow/<policy>.yaml policy files (gates first, optional experts)
new.role: data, not prompts, for what 'releasable' means per launch

modified.change: replace the self-declared '✅ completed / run /sdd-done' ending with: record completion receipt → emit work.completed (head-bound) → print 'held: awaiting verdict'; both twins
extend the receipt into a work.completed emission (stdlib JSON line with a stdlib-computed event_id, or host-side append from the Stop hook)
run the check script before §5/§7; abort with write_hook_context + on_failure on any non-zero; no --force path; same edit in the Codex skill and the shipped asset; contract test
add the new kinds and payload models; reducer learns verdict: pages / edges
add --escrow[=policy]; feature_launcher writes the escrow enablement and the launch_id the verdict must reference
derive an escrow state (awaiting_verdict | approved @sha | rescheduled | escalated) for /sdd-status
optional: an escrow.notify builtin reusing telegram.send / push.send to announce held / escalated states

untouched: /pr-review and the worker's code-reviewer (review layer stays as is)
close_task.py task.closed semantics and the per-task index stamping
.parrot/sdd_hooks.toml semantics (escrow is not a repo-opt-in hook)
HumanInteractionManager, Teams/Telegram channels, Squawk, Roost, navigator_eventbus (v2 transports only)

patterns.pattern: FEAT-703: promote a decision table into one script; twins branch solely on its exit code; contract test pins the doc surface
FEAT-764 pending → record → finalize for host-dispatched agent work (unrecorded pending = failure)
worker_notification receipt: all-tasks-done precondition, 40-hex HEAD, atomic 0600 write, one-shot host consumption
review_checkpoint: facts resolved locally via git, never from a caller-supplied SHA; exit 3 on stale
LedgerService.acknowledge: human-only decisions refuse non-human: actors; GitCommitApprovalAdapter: trust an approval through the commit that recorded it
FEAT-709 --verdict runners fail closed and honour a deadline

risks.risk: Verdict spoofing: the worker can append escrow.approved with actor human:/agent:escrow to the same journal it already writes task.closed to.
risks.impact: separation of powers would be nominal
risks.mitigation: host-only launch secret (not mounted in the sandbox) included in the verdict's hash, or verify the verdict through a host-recorded artifact the sandbox cannot write; decision U2

risks.risk: Stale verdicts: §4.5 lint reflows and §7 stamping commit on the feature branch during /sdd-done.
risks.impact: every verdict stale at gate time if the gate runs after a commit
risks.mitigation: gate before any closeout commit; compare against HEAD at gate time; re-run escrow on head move

risks.risk: Cross-machine visibility is eventual: a verdict in the local journal is invisible elsewhere until exported and imported.
risks.mitigation: v1 same-host; guard reads local + committed logs; document that verdicts ride the outbox

risks.risk: Index reducer and shareable filter must learn new kinds without triggering the rebuild path.
risks.impact: wiped spec:/task: pages or verdicts silently dropped
risks.mitigation: incremental sync only; explicit is_shareable decision; reducer tests

risks.risk: Judge launched by the operator's own host session (FEAT-764 shape).
risks.impact: independent of the worker, not of the operator
risks.mitigation: state it; v2 can run the judge as a detached tmux session or service

risks.impact: ESCALATE_HITL has no live bidirectional channel
risks.mitigation: v1 = notify builtins + parrot sdd escrow approve|reject

unknowns.question: Where does the held state (AWAITING_VERDICT) live? There is no worker state.json today (C10).
plausible_answers: a) a projection of ledger events (held = work.completed for HEAD without a later escrow.approved for the same HEAD), with only escrow.enabled/policy/launch_id written into the per-spec index header at launch — single source of truth, no dual write (recommended)
b) an escrow block in the per-spec index header mirrored on every verdict (brainstorm's choice)
c) a new sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/escrow.json beside the research state
unknowns.user_answer: ledger projection: held = work.completed for HEAD without a later escrow.approved for the same HEAD; only escrow:{enabled,policy,launch_id} in the index header at launch

unknowns.question: What must 'signed' mean for v1, given the ledger has no signatures and actor strings are self-declared (C6, C7)?
plausible_answers: a) process separation + a host-only launch secret folded into the verdict event (the sandbox cannot read it; the gate recomputes it)
b) GitCommitApprovalAdapter-style: the verdict must be committed on the ledger branch by a host process, gate verifies the commit
c) actor prefix convention only (escrow:/human:), accepted as v1 with spoofing noted
unknowns.user_answer: host-only launch secret: per-launch secret outside the sandbox mounts; verdict carries HMAC over feature_id|launch_id|head_sha|decision; gate recomputes it

unknowns.question: Is there any human override of a missing or negative verdict in /sdd-done, and if so what shape?
plausible_answers: a) no flag at all: the only release is a human: escrow.human_decision=approve recorded via parrot sdd escrow approve --reason (keeps the 'gate takes no force parameter' rule)
c) no override; escalation must be resolved by RESCHEDULE
unknowns.user_answer: human decision event only: no /sdd-done flag; `parrot sdd escrow approve <FEAT> --reason` records a human: escrow.human_decision for the current HEAD

unknowns.question: Who produces the v1 verdict? The owner's framing ('release escrow, not review') suggests gates over diff re-reading.
plausible_answers: a) deterministic gates only in v1 (tests, lint, scope-completeness, head integrity, review-checkpoint present); LLM experts are a policy opt-in
b) a read-only .claude/agents/sdd-escrow.md judge launched by the host after work.completed, FEAT-764 agent-hook shape
c) an in-process AgentRegistry bot (brainstorm's EscrowAgent) — a different runtime from the SDD agents
unknowns.user_answer: host-launched read-only judge agent (.claude/agents/sdd-escrow.md) on top of deterministic gates; launched by the worker's host-side Stop hook (worker_notification.handle_stop); manual fallback `parrot sdd escrow run`

unknowns.question: When escrow is NOT enabled for a launch, does the worker keep today's self-declared ending, or does it always emit work.completed with /sdd-done only enforcing the verdict when escrow.enabled?
plausible_answers: a) always emit work.completed (cheap, uniform audit trail); enforcement only when enabled (recommended)
b) emit only when enabled; behaviour unchanged otherwise
unknowns.user_answer: always emit work.completed; /sdd-done enforces the gate only when the launch recorded escrow.enabled

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence; the brainstorm settled the architecture; U1-U5 resolved by the owner on 2026-11-07 (ledger projection, HMAC launch secret, human decision event only, Stop-hook-launched read-only judge, always emit work.completed).

meta.notes: overall_confidence is medium because the scope hinges on U1 (state location) and U2 (what signed means). Rule 8 would map medium to sdd-brainstorm, but the input already is a brainstorm; recommending sdd-spec with the unknowns carried as Open Questions. Mode resolved to enrichment: the source is additive (construir, emitir, held/release). Research was not truncated.
